context_requirements: Functional glucagon receptor (GCGR) expression on the cell surface
Active glucagon/cAMP/PKA signaling tone to antagonize
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
A shared transcriptional signature across multiple lines that tracks with GCGR antagonist treatment
Evidence of GCGR expression and glucagon-responsive cAMP signaling in these lines

evidence.supports: GCGR antagonism primarily affects hepatic glucose and amino acid metabolism; transcriptional effects were observed in monkey liver, not in the tested human cell lines
Peptide GCGR antagonist altered islet alpha/beta-cell turnover in mice but showed no systemic metabolic transcriptional response in the tested context
Glucagon receptor signaling is studied in monocytes/macrophages and vasculature, not in the nine profiled cancer cell lines
